t: For necessary expenses in carrying out science, mathematics and engineering education and human resources programs and activities pursuant to the National Science Foundation Act of 1950 (42 U.S.C. 1861 et seq.), including services as authorized by section 3109 of title 5, United States Code, authorized travel, and rental of conference rooms in the District of Columbia, $895,610,000, to remain available until September 30, 2014:  Provided, That not less than $54,890,000 shall be available until expended for activities authorized by section 7030 of Public Law 110–69.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision funding National Science Foundation education and human resources programs. The tempting reading is that authorizing section 3109 services (temporary experts and consultants) and conference room rental implies outside consultation, but that is only spending authority to procure services and space. Nothing requires or recommends that any outside party be consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge a federal decision.
fable.s: including services as authorized by section 3109 of title 5, United States Code, authorized travel, and rental of conference rooms in the District of Columbia

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes funding for specific programs and activities. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. The mention of 'programs' refers to the subject of the spending, not a participatory mechanism.
qwen_block.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out science, mathematics and engineering education and human resources programs and activities pursuant to the National Science Foundation Act of 1950 (42 U.S.C. 1861 et seq.), including services as authorized by section 3109 of title 5, United States Code, authorized travel, and rental of conference rooms in the District of Columbia, $895,610,000, to remain available until September 30, 2014: Provided, That not less than $54,890,000 shall be available until expended for activities authorized by section 7030 of Public Law 110–69.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "science, mathematics and engineering education and human resources programs" inherently involve the public or outside experts, so this must be participation. However, the text itself is purely an appropriation clause specifying funding amounts and availability dates. It does not describe any specific mechanism for outside parties to consult, comment, or coordinate with the federal government before a decision is made. It simply authorizes spending.

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that funds National Science Foundation education programs and says what the money can be spent on. The reference to section 3109 of title 5 lets the agency pay for temporary expert and consultant services, which works like employment rather than outside participation in a federal decision. Renting conference rooms is also just a spending item. No comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: including services as authorized by section 3109 of title 5, United States Code, authorized travel, and rental of conference rooms in the District of Columbia

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes funding for specific programs. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties, nor does it create advisory bodies or public comment periods. The mention of 'programs' is generic and does not specify participatory mechanisms.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out science, mathematics and engineering education and human resources programs and activities pursuant to the National Science Foundation Act of 1950 (42 U.S.C. 1861 et seq.), including services as authorized by section 3109 of title 5, United States Code, authorized travel, and rental of conference rooms in the District of Columbia, $895,610,000, to remain available until September 30, 2014: Provided, That not less than $54,890,000 shall be available until expended for activities authorized by section 7030 of Public Law 110–69.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "science, mathematics and engineering education and human resources programs" inherently involve interaction with the public (students, teachers, researchers). However, the text itself is purely an appropriation clause specifying funding amounts and availability. It does not describe any specific mechanism for public participation, consultation, or advisory input. It merely authorizes spending.
